ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows the operation process from left to right: first there is a square sheet of paper, with a vertical dashed line in the middle, and the arrow indicates folding along the vertical midline; next a rectangle is obtained, with a horizontal dashed line in the middle, and the arrow indicates folding again along the horizontal midline; finally a smaller square folded paper stack is obtained, with a vertical line and a horizontal line drawn on it, and scissors are used to mark cutting open along these two lines. Reasoning: After two folds, the final small square represents one fourth of the original square, and there are four layers of paper. The two cutting lines in the figure will pass through four layers of paper at the same time. When unfolded, the vertical cutting line on the final small square will be symmetrically copied with respect to the first vertical crease, forming two vertical cutting lines in the original square; the horizontal cutting line will be symmetrically copied with respect to the second horizontal crease, forming two horizontal cutting lines in the original square. Therefore the original square is divided by 2 vertical cutting lines and 2 horizontal cutting lines into 3 columns times 3 rows, a total of 9 pieces.

method.method_draft: Use an unfolding-symmetry model. First read the diagram: the square is folded once along its vertical middle line, then the resulting rectangle is folded along its horizontal middle line, so the final folded stack represents one quarter of the original square. On this folded stack, the picture shows two straight cuts: one vertical through the folded square and one horizontal through the folded square. Treat each cut as being made through all four layers. When the paper is unfolded, the vertical cut in the quarter-square is mirrored across the first fold to give two vertical cut lines in the original square, and the horizontal cut is mirrored across the second fold to give two horizontal cut lines. Thus the unfolded square is divided by 2 vertical and 2 horizontal full cut lines into a 3-by-3 grid, giving 9 pieces.
